messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for hosted-api in eu-west1 (metric: inference.errors.per_min > 200) - triggered at 2024-07-26T05:12:00Z
maya (oncall): taking it - paging now. seeing 502/503 from edge->inference mesh in eu-west1.
jordan (sre): acked. can you post the customer visible impact? do we have any degraded fallbacks enabled?
maya (oncall): quick check: control-plane shows healthy, serving nodes in eu-west1 showing connection drops to the model workers (gRPC stream resets). traffic spike ~x3 on short seq workloads.
lee (platform): possible egress networking flaps between eu-west1 AZs, we had a cloud maint window earlier but no incident flagged. checking VPC flow logs now.
maya (oncall): ops-alerts shows autoscaler tried to spin up 4 extra pods but they fail readiness due to kv-cache reconnect timeouts.
jordan (sre): mitigation plan: 1) carve a temporary routing rule to prefer eu-central1 for new requests 2) enable degraded-mode (no streaming) for long-poll requests in eu-west1 3) scale dedicated fallback pool for critical customers. anyone object?
lee (platform): agree. I can flip the route. command: `redwoodctl route set --service hosted-api --region eu-west1 --fallback eu-central1 --weight 0.0`
maya (oncall): doing it now. will also set short TTL on routing to be reversible.
maya (oncall): `> redwoodctl route set ...` response: ok - new route pushed, traffic should start shifting within 30s.
ops-alerts: SYSTEM: Reroute active - 85% of new connections are now being sent to eu-central1.
sam (product-support): heads-up for support: customers in EU may see increased latency and token truncation on streaming. preparing canned response for status page / support channel.
jordan (sre): next: enable degraded mode in eu-west1 to reduce reconnection churn. maya can you flip feature-flag `streaming_degraded_mode` in eu-west1?
maya (oncall): setting flag: `flags.set --env eu-west1 streaming_degraded_mode true` -> applied.
lee (platform): i've also temporarily increased LB retries to 3 for eu-west1->eu-central1 path and bumped connect timeout to 10s. watching NLB metrics.
jordan (sre): rolling healthcheck script to kill flapping worker pods to let autoscaler replace them: `kubectl -n inference label pods -l region=eu-west1 flapping=true` then drain. proceeding.
maya (oncall): running drain now.
ops-alerts: NOTE: Customers with pinned model versions in eu-west1 may still be routed to older pools; consider advising them.
sam (product-support): draft status page update (please review):
```
Status: Major outage - Partial service degradation in eu-west1
Updated: 2024-07-26T05:38:00Z
Impact: Some hosted API requests originating in EU (eu-west1) may receive 5xx errors or elevated latency. We are currently routing new traffic to eu-central1 as a temporary mitigation.
Workaround: No action required for most customers; traffic will be rerouted automatically. Customers with regional pinning should contact support for assistance.
Next update: in 15 minutes or when there is a status change.
```
lee (platform): looks good. add note about potential increased cross-region egress costs while reroute is active.
sam (product-support): added note. finalizing. sending to status page now.
maya (oncall): posting customer notification to #support now: `We are aware of an issue affecting EU hosted inference (eu-west1). We are rerouting traffic to eu-central1 and mitigating. Expect intermittent errors and higher latency. ETA for full recovery TBD.`
jordan (sre): parallel mitigation: spinning up emergency dedicated pool in eu-central1 and temporarily increasing capacity for critical customers (partner tier & enterprise).
maya (oncall): dedicated pool spin-up succeeded for 3 emergency pools. capacity healthy.
ops-alerts: METRIC: 5xx rate in eu-west1 decreased from 18% -> 6% since reroute; overall request volume in eu-central1 increased by 28%.
jordan (sre): good signal. next steps: keep reroute, continue draining flapping workers, follow up with network team to confirm underlying egress issue, and prepare post-incident customer blurb.
lee (platform): contacting cloud NOC now and requesting network trace for AZ routing between eu-west1-a/b. I will paste their ticket id when assigned.
maya (oncall): handing off to jordan for overlap with morning shift. jordan, I left runbook steps in incident docs and flagged top customers in PagerDuty list.
jordan (sre): taking over. i'll coordinate the long-term fix and prepare the postmortem. thanks maya.
sam (product-support): copying final customer-notice draft for review before broadcast: `We experienced a partial outage affecting hosted inference in eu-west1 leading to elevated errors and latency. Traffic has been rerouted to eu-central1 as a temporary mitigation. We are continuing to restore full service in eu-west1 and will follow up with a detailed incident report.` anyone have wording tweaks?
lee (platform): add: "We apologize for the disruption; if you have pinning or compliance requirements preventing cross-region failover, please open a ticket and we will assist."
sam (product-support): added. publishing to status.redwood.ai now.
ops-alerts: SYSTEM: Status page updated at 2024-07-26T05:45:20Z.
jordan (sre): summary for internal comms template: 1) incident id: INC-20240726-EU-EGRESS 2) affected regions: eu-west1 (primary), eu-central1 (fallback, no outage) 3) scope: Hosted API - partial 5xx/errors for EU-origin traffic, impact mitigated by reroute 4) cause: suspected cloud egress/fabric instability (under investigation) 5) mitigation: traffic reroute, degraded streaming flag, drained flapping pods, emergency pools spun up 6) customer impact: intermittent 5xx and higher latencies for EU customers; customers with region pinning may be impacted until manual assist 7) next steps: network NOC report, postmortem, and customer follow-up.
maya (oncall): thanks. i'll stay available for any escalation for 30m then sign out.
jordan (sre): noted. i'll own the follow-up and postmortem. closing handoff.
ops-alerts: RESOLVE: Primary error spike reduced to baseline; monitoring in watch state. Incident status: mitigated - under investigation.
maya (oncall): thx team.
